These are judgment-based estimates. I did not run any analysis, because the benchmark table is not available in the working directory.

**Assumptions behind the estimates:**
- **Learning rate:** the high band (0.0774 to 1) probably makes training fail. So steps that stabilise training help most there: lowering the learning rate (pair 21) and a larger batch (pair 3).
- **L2 penalty:** in an sklearn-style MLP, the penalty is divided by the batch size, so regularisation is stronger with small batches. That should make alpha changes matter more at small batch sizes (pairs 28 and 29).
- **High alpha and depth:** large alpha (0.129 to 1) underfits, and that likely gets worse with more layers (pairs 12, 13, 23 and 27).
- **Other pairs:** most of the rest should show no interaction that is consistent across all three datasets, so they lean towards N.
